title: Fast fallback token quarantine workstream notes
content:
One-line summary: Fast-fallback token quarantine is a lightweight operational pattern to isolate likely-compromised API credentials quickly, while preserving customer traffic via soft quota bridging and degraded-but-available routes. This doc captures the playtest plan, observed signals, draft runbook steps, and post-playtest telemetry gaps. Context / why this workstream exists: - We face repeated short-lived credential exfiltration bursts that blast our hosted API rate limits and can trigger downstream SLA violations for other customers. - Existing hard-block workflows (rotate key + customer outreach) are effective but too slow at scale and result in collateral outages for legitimate sessions tied to the token. - Goal: enable SRE to rapidly quarantine an API token into a low-bandwidth, high-scrutiny lane where requests are allowed but tightly shaped (soft quota), with automatic heuristics to re-evaluate and either escalate to full revoke or release back to normal. What we playtested (summary): - Trigger: high token QPS relative to moving baseline (>20x recent 10m median) + anomalous IP churn + evidence of malformed prompt patterns (repeated single-word generation). - Action: automated policy applied to token -> mark token state = QUARANTINED; route traffic to quarantine cluster that enforces: 5 rps per token, strict KV cache bypass, insert challenge header X-Quarantine:1, WAF stricter rule-set (rate-based signature tier 3). - Soft quota bridging: allow up to 1% of prior 1h volume to route through low-cost fallback variants (quantized models) to preserve essential flows (webhooks, admin APIs). Timeline (brief playtest run on 2026-02-16): - 14:03: detection: surge detector alerted (token_rate_anom_v2). - 14:04: auto-policy evaluated: anomalous_ip_score=0.81, prompt_entropy_z=-2.6, 1m qps=1200 (baseline 45). - 14:04: quarantine action executed by orchestration service (orchestrator-v2). - 14:04-14:06: observed 83% reduction in backend request spikes due to per-token shaping; latency for quarantined token rose ~120ms median (expected). - 14:10: oncall reviewed and left quarantine in place. - 14:27: automated heuristic re-evaluated: ip_churn decreased, but prompt entropy remained low -> remained quarantined. - 15:30: manual escalation: SRE rotated and replaced token after customer confirmed key leak. Signals that reliably triggered quarantine in playtest: - Sustained qps > 15x baseline for 2 consecutive 1m windows. - Rapid ephemeral IP diversity: >40 unique client IPs within 5m combined with low successful-response-rate ratio. - Prompt shape signatures: repeated near-identical generations with short outputs.
(We used the new prompt-shape extractor hash v0.3). False positives observed: - Multi-tenant CI systems that fan out short bursts of traffic from many ephemeral IPs but with valid diversions (legit product tests). - CDN misconfigurations where multiple egress NATs appeared as high churn. Mitigations to reduce FP risk: - Add slow-start grace: require qps > 15x for at least 90s across sliding windows before auto-quarantine. - Cross-check with customer plan: customers flagged as "integration-testing" in billing metadata get expanded thresholds. - IP reputation lookup (fast cache) to discount known multi-e2e test harnesses. Draft runbook steps (fast-fallback flow) - short checklist for oncall: 1) Detection: receive token_quarantine alert in SRE channel (pager or slack alert). Check telemetry page for token id, qps trend, unique_ips, avg_response_success_ratio, prompt_shape_hash. 2) Quick triage (1–3 min): confirm detection via Winston dashboards + request sample from tracing storage. If false positive -> run UNQUARANTINE policy (button: revert-quarantine) and annotate incident. 3) If likely compromise: trigger QUARANTINE (if not auto-applied) from orchestrator UI -> this attaches header X-Quarantine:1 and switches routing to quarantine cluster. 4) Apply soft quota bridging: set per-token rps limit (default 5rps) and allow fallback model routing for up to 1% historical 1h volume. 5) Notify Customer Success (CS) via template message with subject: "Potential key compromise - temporary mitigation applied" and include mitigation actions and next steps. 6) If customer confirms leak or telemetry indicates credential export, rotate token via API-key-service (rotate-key endpoint) and move to full revoke. 7) Post-incident: run forensics (download request traces, IP lists, prompt samples), create incident ticket (SRV-xxx), and schedule detective work for telemetry gaps. Operational knobs we used in playtest (config keys): - quarantine.rps_per_token (int) -> default 5 - quarantine.volume_window_pct -> default 1 (percent) - quarantine.ip_churn_threshold -> default 40 (unique IPs / 5m) - quarantine.prompt_entropy_z -> default -2.5 - quarantine.grace_seconds -> default 90 - quarantine.waf_profile -> tier3-strict - quarantine.fallback_model_list -> [redwood-llama-q4_8b, redwood-tiny-embed-q2] (list managed in console) WAF tuning notes (what changed during playtest): - Enabled dynamic rate-based signatures (look for repeated identical request bodies) -> reduced noise from legitimate short requests by scoring client behavior, not just payload content. - Added a temporary fingerprint signature to detect the specific SDK pattern used by the suspected bot farm (user-agent + sequence-of-endpoints). This signature should be ephemeral and tied to the incident id. - Important: avoid blanket 403s; quarantine flow keeps requests allowed but throttled so WAF should prefer scoring + challenge (CAPTCHA-equivalent header) vs block. Telemetry gaps and instrumentation asks (post-playtest): - We need token->customer mapping in request trace logs (currently redacted for PII reasons). Add masked customer id field for SRE-only traces. - Add sample payload capture for quarantined tokens (sampling 0.1%) to central forensic store for 7d retention. - Expose quarantine policy decision reason in alert payload (fields: reason_score, contributing_signals) to speed triage. - Add a delta-metric: post-quarantine backend qps (to validate expected mitigation) to the main incident dashboard. Playtest learnings & recommendations: - Fast quarantine materially reduces backend spike surface area and buys time for full key rotation without causing complete outage for small legitimate flows. - Soft quota bridging avoids urgent escalations for some customers (they kept critical webhooks alive) but needs clear CS messaging to avoid confusion. - The grace_window and customer-plan checks are essential: initial auto-trigger parameters were too aggressive for integration-heavy customers. - The WAF signature approach is useful but must be kept ephemeral and instrumented with exact disable time to prevent permanent noise. Unresolved questions / open action items (owner, due): - Decide default quarantine.rps_per_token for enterprise vs free-tier (owner: Sophie Nguyen, due: 2026-02-25). - Add trusted-caller list exclusion logic to orchestration (owner: Arjun Patel, due: 2026-02-22). - Implement trace-level masked customer id and add to SRE read-only logs (owner: Daniel Ruiz, PR open: infra#4123, due: 2026-03-05). - Create CS message templates and automation for notifying customers when their keys are quarantined (owner: Leah Kim, due: 2026-02-24). - Run a false-positive audit against last 6 months of traffic to tune thresholds (owner: eng-sre analytics, due: 2026-03-10). Notes to self / shortcuts used during playtest (informal): - Orchestrator quick command: /orchestrator quarantine --token --reason "auto:rate_anom_v2" --ttl 24h - Dashboard: Winston -> Token Overview -> Quarantine pane -> links to traces (time window auto-populated) - Slack thread: #sre-abuse-ops pinned incident snippets for 02/16 playtest - Small TODO: add a per-token cooldown label in the Console to show last_quarantine_ts. Appendix: example Slack template for CS (replace placeholders): "Hi , we detected unusual activity on one of your API keys and temporarily placed it into a low-bandwidth quarantine to protect your account and our service. This action preserves small essential traffic while we investigate. If you recognize this activity, please confirm and we will lift the quarantine. If not, we recommend rotating the key immediately. SRE has applied a soft fallback to minimize disruption to critical traffic. — SRE team" End of notes. This remains a working doc; please add more playtest results and incident ids below as we run more experiments.
